Daily Brief

World leaders convened in New York on Tuesday for the UN General Assembly's annual high-level debate, with some 130 heads of state expected to address conflicts in Iran, Ukraine, Sudan, and Yemen, alongside concerns over AI governance and climate change [RFI]. Presidents Macron and Trump held what the French leader described as 'very constructive' talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and pursuing an 'energy truce' between Russia and Ukraine amid surging oil prices [RFI, France 24]. The G7 foreign ministers issued a joint statement demanding Iran cease arming the Houthis in Yemen, warning that recent escalation threatens regional and global energy security [BBC]. Major US television networks suspended pooled coverage of the White House after CNN, Politico and MS NOW were barred, prompting the administration to launch its own streaming channel, Trump TV [BBC]. A joint investigation by RFI and 23 media outlets revealed the US has deported over 25,000 people to third countries since Trump's return to power, with some sent to African nations where they face detention without legal status [RFI, The Guardian]. In Turkey, an 11-person shooting outside a high school in Manisa marked the country's third such incident this year [BBC, Al Jazeera].

02 Geopolitics

Macron and Trump Discuss Reopening Strait of Hormuz and Ukraine Energy Truce

  • French President Macron met with President Trump in New York ahead of the UN General Assembly, describing talks as 'very constructive'
  • Macron proposed measures to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted since the outbreak of war involving Iran, Israel and the US in February
  • Paris seeks a UN Security Council resolution guaranteeing freedom of navigation through the strait, which normally carries 20% of global oil and gas trade
  • The leaders also discussed protecting Saudi oil infrastructure and pursuing an 'energy truce' between Russia and Ukraine

G7 Demands Iran Stop Arming Houthis as Yemen Conflict Escalates

  • G7 foreign ministers issued a joint statement calling on Iran to 'end its arming of and support' for the Houthis in Yemen
  • The statement condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and warned the escalation threatens regional and global energy security

04 Policy

Major US Networks Suspend Pooled White House Coverage After Media Ban

  • Major US television networks suspended pooled coverage of President Trump after CNN, Politico and MS NOW were barred from the White House on Friday
  • The three banned outlets announced they will sue the Trump administration to 'defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports'
  • The White House launched Trump TV, a 24/7 streaming channel featuring clips of the president
  • New York Times and Washington Post declined to share still images from Trump events; no network footage aired of Trump boarding Air Force One or arriving in New York

05 Policy

Investigation Reveals US Deporting Migrants to Third Countries Across Africa

  • More than 25,000 people have been deported from the US to third countries since Trump's return to power, according to a six-month investigation by 24 media outlets
  • At least 12 African countries have agreed to receive deportees, including Central African Republic and Equatorial Guinea
  • Some deportees were sent to countries they have no connection to; others were later sent to places where they risked persecution or torture
  • Witnesses reported deportees in Equatorial Guinea were bound, beaten, and detained in a hotel where about 30 remain trapped
